about.title: Walnut Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products don't announce themselves — a car part fails on La Puente Road, a tool malfunctions in a Walnut garage, or a household item causes injury during ordinary use. Under California's strict liability rules, the person hurt generally doesn't need to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective in design, manufacturing, or warning, and that the defect caused the injury. That's a meaningful difference from many other injury claims, and it opens the door to holding manufacturers, distributors, and retailers accountable together. Walnut sits in Los Angeles County, where product cases can involve local retailers as well as national manufacturers. If a defective product hurt you or someone you love here, keeping the item itself — unaltered, if possible — matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect Walnut residents, free of charge, with an independent attorney who reviews the details and explains options on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Claim

items.title: No Need to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: Under California's strict liability standard, you generally don't have to show the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may broaden who can be pursued for a claim.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Case
items.desc: Keeping the defective item as-is, rather than repairing or discarding it, helps preserve evidence an attorney may need to evaluate design, manufacturing, or warning defects.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability approach generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and whether that defect caused your injury, rather than what the manufacturer knew. An independent attorney can walk through the specifics of your situation and explain how this might apply.

items.question: I was hurt by a product I bought at a store near Grand Avenue in Walnut. Can the store be responsible too?
items.answer: Retailers can sometimes share liability alongside manufacturers and distributors under California product liability principles, depending on the circumstances. This is one of the reasons it helps to have an attorney review exactly where and how the product was sold. LawProactive can connect you with someone free of charge to look into it.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened — don't repair, alter, or throw it away. The product itself is often key evidence in a defect claim. An independent attorney can advise on how to document and preserve it properly.
